title: Subtracting Numbers up to 100 without Regrouping
seo_title: Grade 1 Subtracting within 100 Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 1)
standard_text: Subtract numbers where both numbers are less than 100 using concrete and pictorial models, without regrouping: a. 2-digit minus 1-digit numbers, and b. 2-digit minus 2-digit numbers; subtract numbers by expressing minuends and subtrahends as tens and ones (expanded form), without regrouping.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 worksheets on subtracting within 100 without regrouping for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: tens and ones, expanded form and stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Ones from ones, tens from tens.
key_sub: Check: answer + number taken away = start.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Subtract the ones from the ones and the tens from the tens.
  • 48 − 5: 8 − 5 = 3 ones, 4 tens. The answer is 43.
  • 68 − 25: 8 − 5 = 3 ones, 6 − 2 = 4 tens. The answer is 43.
  • Expanded form: 68 − 25 = (60 − 20) + (8 − 5) = 40 + 3 = 43.

Examples

Example

79 − 34

ones: 9 − 4 = 5

tens: 7 − 3 = 4

Answer: 45

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Ones from tensLine up the ones with the ones.
Adding“Left” means subtract.
Forgetting the tensSubtract the tens too.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 1 ask about subtracting to 100?
faq.a: Subtract numbers where both numbers are less than 100 without regrouping (2-digit minus 1-digit and 2-digit minus 2-digit), and subtract numbers by expressing them as tens and ones.

faq.q: How can I check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number you took away.
Grade 1 learners subtract tens and ones separately first.

items.q: Each rod is 10. Some rods are crossed out. What is 30 − 20?
items.e: There are 3 rods. That is 30. 2 rods are crossed out. Count the rods left: 1 ten. 30 − 20 = 10.

items.q: Each rod is 10. Some rods are crossed out. What is 40 − 10?
items.e: There are 4 rods. That is 40. 1 rod is crossed out. Count the rods left: 3 tens. 40 − 10 = 30.

items.q: Each rod is 10. Some rods are crossed out. What is 40 − 20?
items.e: There are 4 rods. That is 40. 2 rods are crossed out. Count the rods left: 2 tens. 40 − 20 = 20.

items.q: There are 5 tens. 1 ten is crossed out. How many tens are left?

items.e: There are 6 rods. That is 60. 1 rod is crossed out. Count the rods left: 5 tens. 60 − 10 = 50.

items.q: Each rod is 10. Some rods are crossed out. What is 50 − 30?
items.e: There are 5 rods. That is 50. 3 rods are crossed out. Count the rods left: 2 tens. 50 − 30 = 20.
There are 6 rods, so start at 60. 2 rods are crossed out, so take away 20. The picture shows 60 − 20 = 40.

items.q: Each rod is 10. Some rods are crossed out. What is 50 − 40?
items.e: There are 5 rods. That is 50. 4 rods are crossed out. Count the rods left: 1 ten. 50 − 40 = 10.
There are 6 rods. That is 60. 3 rods are crossed out. Count the rods left: 3 tens. 60 − 30 = 30.
Count the tens like ones. 4 − 1 = 3. So 4 tens − 1 ten = 3 tens.
Count the tens like ones. 6 − 2 = 4. So 6 tens − 2 tens = 4 tens.
Count the tens like ones. 5 − 3 = 2. So 5 tens − 3 tens = 2 tens.
40 is 4 tens and 10 is 1 ten. So use 4 − 1.
Count the tens like ones. 7 − 1 = 6. So 7 tens − 1 ten = 6 tens.
80 is 8 tens. 50 is 5 tens. So 80 − 50 is 8 tens − 5 tens.
80 is 8 tens. 30 is 3 tens. So 80 − 30 is 8 tens − 3 tens.
